state:
Goal `core-response-and-1-more`: every body member of `Core\Response` — `addCookie`, `bytes`,
`html`, `text` and `json` — has every feature proof: `about.md`, three examples with `.nvsr`
requests, the attack, the bench record in `docs/perf/members.ndjson`, and a `covers:` line on
`each_body_member_sets_its_own_content_type` in `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/response.rs`. The
`BYTES_DOC`, `HTML_DOC`, `TEXT_DOC` and `JSON_DOC` cards follow AGENTS.md § *Text an end user
reads*. The cards of `setStatus`, `setHeader`, `redirect` and `sendFile` do not yet.
`Core\Response\Stream` is still in `CLASSES_STILL_OWING_A_CARD` in
`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/registry.rs`, and `Core\Response\Stream::write` owes every proof. Nothing is
blocked.

`nvs run --request` prints the response body alone, never the status line or the headers, so an
example about a status or a header shows it through the body it writes. A body member's bench
writes bodies with no newline in them, because a newline flushes the terminal on every call. The
wall-clock of these benches is noisy: compare the allocation and byte counts.

items.text: **`Core\Response::setStatus`** — owes examples, hostile, perf, Rust `covers:` (`rule:security/response-body-is-one-typed-member`). Member at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/response.rs:1134`, card at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/response.rs:721`. The body is all an example can show, so each one writes a body saying what status it chose.

**`Core\Response::setHeader`** — the same owed set. Member at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/response.rs:1175`, card at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/response.rs:740`. The attack is header injection through the name and the value, and `Content-Type` in any case.
**`Core\Response::redirect`** — the same owed set. Member at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/response.rs:1244`, card at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/response.rs:769`.

backlog: `Core\Response\Stream::write` owes every proof and its class a card — `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/registry.rs` `CLASSES_STILL_OWING_A_CARD`; acceptance check `dossier-core-response-stream`.
